item.title: Traffic often running red light turning into South Lambeth Road, 5th September
item.description:
When making the left turn from the main Clapham Road into South Lambeth Road at the Stockwell Memorial Garden junction, I have found that a number of drivers will go through the red light for their direction. There are currently 3 sets of lights, each with their own sequence (1 for going straight along Clapham Road, 1 for left into South Lambeth Road and 1 for the cycle lane to go straight down Clapham Road). A number of times I have had cars jump the first set of lights on the corner before making an abrupt stop once they turn the corner and see people on the crossing who have been given a green light to cross. This has happened at different points of the day across the short time I’ve been living in the area but would not be able to say how long this has been an issue for. I believe more should be done in terms of visibility for drivers as for pedestrians that are unable to move as quickly or anticipate a car travelling around the corner, it could be dangerous. I will note that there are secondary lights which cars I have encountered will stop at but they must do so very abruptly as they do not anticipate another set of lights considering they have gone through 1 set albeit wrongly.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Clapham Road, Stockwell, Greater London

item.title: Crossing safety issues on side roads either side of Cromwell Road., 4th September
item.description:
There are no crossing lights visible to pedestrians on many of the side roads leading to Cromwell Road, including the gardens (numerous roads named ... gardens) and those north of the road. Specifically within a mile west of South Kensington Station. This has turned out extremely dangerous for many people - I've both nearly been and witnessed others nearly been run over while crossing these side roads, because we can't see whether the cars have red or green and we have no lights of our own. Vehicles frequently whizz through these roads so they can't be seen before crossing, especially in evenings. This issue has been present for at least 2 years, and it seems like an accident waiting to happen.
Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): 1, Stanhope Gardens, Brompton, Greater London

item.title: Debris on the curbs, blocked drains, overgrown hedges, 4th September
item.description:

The public drains are full of dead leaves etc so when we get a heavy downpour they overflow, making it even more dangerous for us. The public hedges (x3) are so overgrown that they can block someone hiding behind it which is dangerous for the females that live in Whitstable Close plus they drip water onto you as you walk past them. We have a number of elderly and disabled pple living in the close and its extremely dangerous for us
